summary: Iteration 5 focused on the user-reported bug 'Google review link save shows an error'. Backend: extended /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py to 59 pytest cases (new class TestGoogleUrlValidator + TestPublic::test_use_returns_exact_saved_google_url + TestBusinessImages::test_reject_renamed_non_image), 57 passed / 2 failed. The fix itself is confirmed working: PUT /api/settings now accepts and persists https://g.page/r/CVxyz123/review, https://g.page/{name}/review, https://maps.app.goo.gl/AbCdEf, https://g.co/kgs/abc123, https://search.google.com/local/writereview?placeid=ChIJabc, https://www.google.co.in/maps/place/X, https://share.google/xyz, schemeless g.page/r/CVx/review (stored as https://...) and http:// links (upgraded to https). Non-Google hosts (example.com, google.com.evil.com, evil.com/?x=google.com, notgoogle.com, ggoogle.com) return 422 with the friendly message and the stored value is unchanged. Empty value saves and sets is_active=false. GOOGLE_RE is fully removed. The 2 failures are a NEW security finding (host-spoofing bypass, see backend_issues). Two stale assertions from the old behaviour were updated (error text 'Google review link' -> 'Google link') and the image fixtures were regenerated with PIL because the backend now magic-byte validates uploads (the old truncated base64 test JPEG/PNG was rightly rejected with 422). Frontend (Playwright, preview URL): full My Business save flow verified - g.page/r link -> 'Saved' toast, pill ACTIVE, value persists after reload; all 5 other Google formats -> 'Saved'; schemeless link stored with https://; the 3 non-Google links -> single friendly error toast and the previously saved link unchanged after reload; clearing the field -> 'Saved' + pill 'ADD GOOGLE LINK'; name/category/location/service area persist. E2E: /r/PCiXONhzO_7mFA renders 6 cards, tapping one issues a request to exactly https://g.page/r/CVxyz123/review and the row flips to USED in the dashboard. Regression: reviews list, bulk selection bar ('1 selected / Copy all / Delete all / Clear'), Category list (3), Add Reviews prefill from settings, change-password wrong-current error toast, logout, and logo (200x200 PNG) + shop photo (600x300 JPEG) upload with previews rendering (naturalWidth 200/600) and persisting after reload. The previously reported /settings mobile overflow is fixed (scrollWidth 390 == clientWidth 390 at 390px). Demo account left with google_review_url = https://g.page/r/CVxyz123/review (ACTIVE).

critical.issue: Host-spoofing bypass: host is parsed by manual string splitting (split('//')[1].split('/')[0].split('?')[0].split('@')[-1]), which ignores the URL fragment and backslashes. 'https://evil.com#@google.com/' and 'https://evil.com\\@g.page/r/x/review' are ACCEPTED and stored (200), yet browsers resolve both to host evil.com - so a stored phishing URL is what customers get redirected to from the public page. Fix: use urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname (reject if None) and validate that, instead of manual splitting. Reproduced by pytest TestGoogleUrlValidator::test_host_spoofing_rejected (2 failing cases).

minor.issue: Links with an explicit port ('https://google.com:8080/x') are rejected because the port is not stripped before the host allow-list check - harmless today but inconsistent with urlsplit-based parsing.
Still only $unset of {kind}_path; the stored object is never deleted from object storage and {kind}_content_type stays behind (open from iteration 4).
logo_url/photo_url still lack the ?v={version} cache-buster while the image route sends Cache-Control: max-age=3600 (open from iteration 4).

integration_issues.issue: PublicReview.choose() awaits navigator.clipboard.writeText() BEFORE window.location.href; if the clipboard API is unavailable/denied (non-secure context, older mobile browser, permission denied) the whole flow falls into catch and the customer is never redirected to Google - only a 'Please tap again to copy your review' toast is shown, and the review has already been marked USED by the API call. Reproduced by running the tap without clipboard permission granted. Suggest wrapping the clipboard write in its own try/catch so the redirect always happens.

action_items: Replace the manual host parsing in normalise_google_url with urllib.parse.urlsplit(...).hostname (and strip the port) so fragment/backslash spoofs like https://evil.com#@google.com/ and https://evil.com\\@g.page/r/x/review are rejected
In PublicReview.choose(), isolate navigator.clipboard.writeText() in its own try/catch so a clipboard failure never blocks the redirect to the Google review URL
(carry-over) delete the previous storage object and $unset {kind}_content_type on image remove/replace; add ?v= to the public payload image URLs
critical_code_review_comments: normalise_google_url does its own URL parsing - security-sensitive host checks should always use urlsplit().hostname; also note host.endswith('.goo.gl') / '.google.com' allow any subdomain, which is fine for Google but should be documented.

The friendly 422 message is good, but the same validator is not applied anywhere else (no server-side re-validation before redirect on /public/{slug}/use), so any historically stored bad URL keeps being served to customers.
regenerate_review still passes GenerateIn(count=10) then generate_batch(cfg, 1) - dead override (carry-over).
GET /api/public/{slug} still falls back to `visible = [...] or rows`, so a repeat customer can be served an already-used review (carry-over).

rca_of_the_issue: Original user bug: the old GOOGLE_RE regex only matched g.page/{name}/review, so the most common Google Business share link https://g.page/r/{id}/review produced a 422 and an error toast. The replacement normalise_google_url() host allow-list fixes it - verified via API and UI for 9 link shapes. New defect found while probing the new validator: because the host is extracted with manual string splits rather than urlsplit(), a fragment ('#@google.com') or a backslash ('\\@g.page') makes the parser read a Google host while the browser resolves the real host (evil.com), so a phishing URL can be saved and later served as the customer redirect target.
